historical_boundary: Sage and Booth specify least circular rotation; our extra choice of lowest original zero-based shift among exactly equal minima and strict nonempty bit validation is an explicit SENS research contract, not attributed to Sage API.

candidate.inputs: one nonempty finite sequence of exact PredicateBit identities 0 and 1, order fixed; an empty sequence is INVALID, bool/float/text input is INVALID
candidate.outputs: pair (lexicographically least length-N cyclic LEFT rotation as a bit sequence, smallest zero-based original left-rotation index k attaining that minimum)
candidate.law: For finite nonempty w of length N, define rotate(w,k)[i]=w[(i+k) mod N]. Choose c=min_lex {rotate(w,k) | 0<=k<N}. Return (c, min {k | rotate(w,k)=c}). No reversal, sorting, primitive-root contraction, incomplete-period padding, byte alignment, or physical carrier framing.

positives.why: same circle with different original phase
two identical least rotations, choose earlier k=1 rather than 3
repeated cyclic minimum at k=2 and k=5; stable source index 2
aperiodic word with prefix period 2, root algorithm is inapplicable
left circular shift, not bit reversal

falsifiers: Returning 0101 shift 3 instead of shift 1 for 1010 violates smallest-offset witness.
Returning 01 (shortest repeated root) instead of the full 4-bit 0101 for 1010 changes the semantic object length.
Returning 01010 for 01010 because its prefix period appears to be 2 misses least full cyclic shift 00101.
Returning reversed 0011 from 1100 without proving a circular shift (or any reverse operation) must reject.
Returning empty word as a valid canonical cyclic phase erases the precondition N>0.
Treating Python True as exact bit 1 silently conflates bool with bit identity in the typed oracle.
Treating physical T5 padding/separators as elements of the cyclic mathematical word is a carrier/semantics violation.
